article_number: Formal Malaysia sukuk entry (BNM SAC Res 11/14/62/63/99/100/105/108)
content:
record_grade=formal (Malaysia second-batch finance, 2026-09-15).

BNM SAC transforms sukuk structuring principles into binding rulings for Islamic finance:
(1) Res 11 (67th mtg 2007-05-03): sukuk ijarah using third-party asset via mudarabah acquisition — not allowed.
(2) Res 14 (70th mtg 2007-09-12): same via sale concept — permissible.
(3) Res 62 (58th mtg 2006-04-27): sukuk ijarah / Shariah shares as tawarruq underlying — permissible; tangible/financial mix required for sukuk ijarah.
(4) Res 63 (67th mtg 2007-05-03): sukuk commodity murabahah via tawarruq — no Shariah objection if ≥3 parties.
(5) Res 99/100: Sukuk BBA underlying/bidding.
(6) Res 105/108: Danajamin guarantee scope and ownership of ijarah underlying asset.
Official compilation: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/9198675/shariah_resolutions_2nd_edition_EN.pdf. SAC page: https://www.bnm.gov.my/committees/sac. Local verification MD5 08e35a8c9aa2faafc5285d8d9d794484.

article_number: Formal Malaysia takaful entry (BNM SAC Res 41/43/46/50/52/55/56/57/59/91)
content:
record_grade=formal (Malaysia second-batch finance, 2026-09-15).

BNM SAC transforms takaful mutual-assistance principles into binding product/governance rulings:
(1) Res 41: tabarru` + wakalah model for takaful/retakaful permissible.
(2) Res 43: wakalah retakaful with wakaf element permissible; tabarru` foundation retained.
(3) Res 46: specific takaful packaged with conventional credit card — not allowed (riba exposure).
(4) Res 50/52/55: fund segregation; PRF surplus distribution; deficit qard/outright transfer.
(5) Res 56/57/59: hibah benefit; nomination/trustee; permissible takaful interest.
(6) Res 91: PA cover on Islamic credit card — ujrah not allowed; hibah free cover OK.
Official: https://www.bnm.gov.my/documents/20124/9198675/shariah_resolutions_2nd_edition_EN.pdf. Local MD5 08e35a8c9aa2faafc5285d8d9d794484. Shared anchor: SH-PRINCIPLE-TAKAFUL-001.

article_number: Formal Malaysia Shariah-compliance governance entry (IFSA ss.28–29)
content:
record_grade=formal (Malaysia second-batch finance, 2026-09-15).

IFSA 2013 (Act 759) Part IV Division 1:
s.28(1) institution must ensure aims/operations/business/activities comply with Shariah at all times.
s.28(2) compliance with a SAC ruling on a matter is deemed compliance with Shariah for that matter.
s.28(3) on discovery of non-compliance: notify Bank & Shariah committee; immediately cease; submit rectification plan within 30 days.
s.28(5) offence: up to 8 years imprisonment and/or RM25 million fine.
s.29 Bank may issue standards on Shariah matters on SAC advice; s.29(2)(a) expressly includes Shariah governance (board/senior management/Shariah committee duties; fit and proper; internal Shariah compliance function).
s.29(6) breach of standards: same maximum penalty scale.
Official AGC reprint (11 Feb 2021) PDF pp.67–69: https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/1691495_BI/11022021%20ACT%20759%20final.pdf

content:
record_grade=formal (Malaysia second-batch finance, 2026-09-15).

IFSA 2013 Part IV Division 2–3 (AGC reprint pp.70–75):
s.30 mandatory Shariah committee; group single-committee with Bank approval; Bank may require approved persons/designated payment system operators to establish.
s.31 appointment needs fit-and-proper standards + prior written Bank approval.
s.32 duties set by Bank standards under s.29(2)(a)(i).
s.33–34 cessation, 14-day notices, replacement appointment.
s.35 accurate complete non-misleading information to committee; confidentiality.
s.36 qualified privilege for good-faith reporting/performance.
s.37–38 Bank-required or Bank-appointed audit on Shariah compliance; costs on institution.

16:114 فَكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ حَلَـٰلًا طَيِّبًا وَٱشْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ
